title: Why carbon owns a whole branch of chemistry

board_content.text: Organic Chemistry = the chemistry of carbon
1828: Wohler makes urea from ammonium cyanate — the 'vital force' idea collapses.
The name 'organic' stuck; the mysticism didn't.
Why one element earns its own branch? Carbon is the LEGO brick of molecules.
Tetravalent (4 bonds) + catenation (C-C chains) → chains, branches, rings of any size.
Add multiple bonds, links to H, O, N, S, halogens, and isomers → millions of compounds.
Three foundational skills
1. Draw it (representation)  2. Classify it (chain/ring, functional group)  3. Family (homologous series).
'Organic' = carbon-containing — except CO, carbonates, carbides, cyanides (inorganic by tradition).

segments_english.text: <curious>Let's start with a definition that sounds simple but hides a great story. Organic chemistry is just the chemistry of carbon compounds. That's it. But the word organic is a historical fossil.

For a long time chemists believed these compounds could only be built inside living things by a mysterious vital force. Then in eighteen twenty-eight, Friedrich Wohler made urea, an unmistakably organic substance, in his lab starting from purely inorganic ammonium cyanate.
That single experiment tore down the wall between living and non-living chemistry. The mysticism died, but the name organic stubbornly stuck around.
So why does one element get an entire branch of chemistry to itself? Think of carbon as the LEGO brick of the molecular world. One brick alone is unremarkable.

But carbon is tetravalent, meaning it forms four bonds, and it happily clips onto other carbons, a property called catenation. Together these let it build chains, branches, and rings of essentially unlimited size.

Now add that carbon can form single, double, and triple bonds, link to hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, sulphur and the halogens, and produce isomers, and you get the millions of distinct compounds that make up fuels, plastics, medicines, and life itself.
So three foundational skills unlock everything that follows in this chapter.

First, draw a molecule efficiently. Second, classify it as chain or ring and by its functional group. And third, place it in a family called a homologous series, because members of a family behave predictably.

One caution before we move on. Today organic simply means carbon-containing, but by pure tradition a few carbon compounds, like the oxides of carbon, carbonates, carbides, and cyanides, are still treated as inorganic.

segments_hinglish.text: <curious>चलो एक definition से शुरू करते हैं जो simple लगती है but एक बड़ी अच्छी story छुपाती है। Organic chemistry का मतलब है carbon compounds की chemistry। बस इतना ही। लेकिन ये word organic एक historical fossil है।

काफ़ी समय तक chemists मानते थे कि ये compounds सिर्फ़ living things के अंदर एक mysterious vital force से बन सकते हैं। फिर eighteen twenty-eight में, Friedrich Wohler ने urea, जो एक बिलकुल organic substance है, अपनी lab में purely inorganic ammonium cyanate से बना दिया।
उस एक experiment ने living और non-living chemistry के बीच की दीवार गिरा दी। Mysticism ख़त्म हो गया, लेकिन नाम organic ज़िद्दी की तरह टिका रह गया।
तो एक अकेले element को पूरी branch क्यों मिलती है? Carbon को molecular world का LEGO brick समझो। अकेली एक brick कोई ख़ास बात नहीं।

लेकिन carbon tetravalent है, यानी चार bonds बनाता है, और ख़ुशी से दूसरे carbons के साथ जुड़ जाता है, इस property को catenation कहते हैं। ये दोनों मिलकर इसे किसी भी size की chains, branches और rings बनाने देते हैं।

अब इसमें जोड़ो कि carbon single, double और triple bonds बना सकता है, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, sulphur और halogens से जुड़ सकता है, और isomers बना सकता है, तो आपको millions of compounds मिलते हैं जो fuels, plastics, medicines और life ख़ुद बनाते हैं।
तो तीन foundational skills इस पूरे chapter को unlock करती हैं।

पहला, molecule को efficiently draw करना। दूसरा, उसे chain या ring और उसके functional group से classify करना। और तीसरा, उसे एक family में रखना जिसे homologous series कहते हैं, क्योंकि family के members predictably behave करते हैं।

आगे बढ़ने से पहले एक caution। आज organic का मतलब बस carbon-containing है, लेकिन pure tradition की वजह से कुछ carbon compounds, जैसे oxides of carbon, carbonates, carbides और cyanides, अब भी inorganic माने जाते हैं।

title: The four pillars: why carbon is special

board_content.text: Four pillars make carbon unique
Pillar 1 — Tetravalence: 4 valence electrons → 4 covalent bonds → stable 3-D frameworks.
Pillar 2 — Catenation: strong, similar-strength C-C bonds let carbon self-link into chains and rings.
Pillar 3 — Multiple bonding & small size: short strong bonds; pi bonds give C=C and C≡C.
Small atom → close approach → strong pi overlap. Bigger atoms can't do this well.
Pillar 4 — Isomerism: the same atoms, arranged many ways, become different compounds.
No other element combines all four — that is the whole source of organic diversity.
Catenation is exceptional, not infinite — very long unbranched chains get unstable.

segments_english.text: Why does carbon, and only carbon, deserve this attention? Four pillars hold up the entire subject, so let's name them clearly.
Pillar one is tetravalence. Carbon has four valence electrons, so it forms four covalent bonds, and that gives it stable, three-dimensional frameworks to build on.

Pillar two is catenation. Carbon's carbon-to-carbon bonds are strong and all of similar strength, so carbon can link to itself again and again, forming long chains and rings that no other element manages.
Pillar three is multiple bonding paired with carbon's small size. Short, strong bonds and the ability to form pi bonds give us double bonds, C double bond C, and triple bonds, C triple bond C.

<curious>Here's the subtle part. Because carbon is a small atom, its p orbitals can approach closely and overlap strongly to make good pi bonds. Larger atoms sit too far apart for that, which is why they rarely catenate well.
Pillar four is isomerism. Take the very same atoms in the very same numbers, arrange them differently, and you get genuinely different compounds. We'll devote a whole subtopic to it.
No other element brings all four of these together at once. That unique combination is the entire reason organic compounds run into the millions.
One honest limit though. Catenation is exceptional but not infinite in practice. Very long unbranched chains become unstable or hard to isolate.

segments_hinglish.text: Carbon, और सिर्फ़ carbon, को इतनी attention क्यों मिलती है? चार pillars पूरे subject को टिकाए रखते हैं, तो चलो उन्हें clearly नाम देते हैं।
Pillar one है tetravalence। Carbon के पास चार valence electrons होते हैं, तो ये चार covalent bonds बनाता है, और यही इसे stable, three-dimensional frameworks देता है।

Pillar two है catenation। Carbon के carbon-to-carbon bonds strong और लगभग बराबर strength के होते हैं, तो carbon ख़ुद से बार-बार जुड़ सकता है, ऐसी long chains और rings बनाकर जो कोई और element नहीं बना पाता।
Pillar three है multiple bonding, carbon के small size के साथ। Short, strong bonds और pi bonds बनाने की ability हमें double bonds, C double bond C, और triple bonds, C triple bond C, देती है।

<curious>अब एक subtle बात। क्योंकि carbon एक small atom है, इसके p orbitals पास आकर strongly overlap कर सकते हैं और अच्छे pi bonds बना सकते हैं। बड़े atoms इतनी दूर होते हैं कि ऐसा नहीं कर पाते, इसीलिए वो अच्छे से catenate नहीं करते।
Pillar four है isomerism। बिलकुल वही atoms, वही numbers में लो, अलग तरह से arrange करो, और आपको सच में अलग compounds मिलते हैं। इस पर हम एक पूरा subtopic देंगे।
कोई और element इन चारों को एक साथ नहीं लाता। यही unique combination पूरी वजह है कि organic compounds millions में पहुँच जाते हैं।
पर एक honest limit भी। Catenation exceptional है but practice में infinite नहीं। बहुत लंबी unbranched chains unstable हो जाती हैं या isolate करना मुश्किल।

segments_english.text: Writing out every atom for a big molecule is exhausting, so chemists use four different drawings for the same molecule. Let's take propan-one-ol as our example throughout.
The complete, or Lewis, formula shows every single atom and every bond. It's wonderfully clear, but for a large molecule it becomes bulky and slow to draw.
The condensed formula strips out most bonds and groups atoms together, like C H three, C H two, C H two, O H. Compact, and still unambiguous.
Look at the board: the same propan-one-ol appears all four ways side by side, so you can see they describe one identical molecule.
The bond-line, or zig-zag, formula is the workhorse. The carbon skeleton is just a zig-zag of lines. Every vertex and every line-end is a carbon, and the hydrogens on carbon are simply understood.
<excited>Burn this in: a vertex is a carbon. Carbon's hydrogens are left off because they're predictable, but heteroatoms like oxygen, nitrogen and the halogens are always written out explicitly.
Finally the three-dimensional wedge-dash formula. A solid wedge points toward you, a hashed wedge points away, and plain lines lie in the plane, so you can read the molecule's real spatial shape.
Every one of these is the same propan-one-ol. You simply pick the drawing that best makes the point you're trying to make.

segments_hinglish.text: बड़े molecule के लिए हर atom लिखना थका देता है, तो chemists एक ही molecule के लिए चार अलग drawings use करते हैं। चलो propan-one-ol को अपना example बनाकर चलते हैं।
Complete, या Lewis, formula हर एक atom और हर bond दिखाता है। बहुत clear होता है, पर बड़े molecule के लिए bulky और slow हो जाता है।
Condensed formula ज़्यादातर bonds हटा देता है और atoms को group कर देता है, जैसे C H three, C H two, C H two, O H। Compact, और फिर भी unambiguous।
Board देखो: वही propan-one-ol चारों तरीक़ों से साथ-साथ दिखाया गया है, ताकि आप देख सको कि ये एक ही identical molecule describe करते हैं।
Bond-line, या zig-zag, formula असली workhorse है। Carbon skeleton बस lines का एक zig-zag है। हर vertex और हर line-end एक carbon है, और carbon पर hydrogens बस समझ लिए जाते हैं।
<excited>ये पक्का याद कर लो: vertex मतलब carbon। Carbon के hydrogens छोड़ दिए जाते हैं क्योंकि वो predictable हैं, पर heteroatoms जैसे oxygen, nitrogen और halogens हमेशा explicitly लिखे जाते हैं।
आख़िर में three-dimensional wedge-dash formula। Solid wedge आपकी तरफ़ आता है, hashed wedge दूर जाता है, और plain lines plane में रहती हैं, ताकि आप molecule की असली spatial shape पढ़ सको।
इनमें से हर एक वही propan-one-ol है। आप बस वो drawing चुनते हो जो आपकी बात सबसे अच्छे से कहती है।

board_content.text: If cyclic: only carbon in the ring (carbocyclic) or a heteroatom present (heterocyclic)?
If carbocyclic: aromatic (benzene-type) or alicyclic (non-aromatic ring)?
Heteroatom beats aromatic: pyridine is heterocyclic first, aromatic second.
Anchors: butane (acyclic) · cyclohexane (alicyclic) · benzene (aromatic) · pyridine (heterocyclic).
Why bother? Reactivity follows class and functional group — classification predicts chemistry.

segments_english.text: Before you touch any reaction, you classify. And classification has a fixed order: settle the carbon skeleton first, then the functional group.
Question one is simply: is the carbon framework an open chain, or a closed ring? Open chain means acyclic; a ring means cyclic.
The board shows the whole family tree. Follow it top to bottom and every organic compound finds exactly one home.
If it's cyclic, ask question two. Does the ring contain only carbon, which makes it carbocyclic, or does it include a non-carbon atom, which makes it heterocyclic?
If it's carbocyclic, one more question. Is it aromatic, meaning a benzene-type ring, or alicyclic, meaning an ordinary non-aromatic ring?
<curious>Watch the priority carefully. If a ring holds a heteroatom, it is heterocyclic first, even if it's also aromatic. Pyridine is the classic case: heterocyclic beats aromatic.
Some anchors to hold onto: butane is acyclic, cyclohexane is a carbocyclic alicyclic ring, benzene is carbocyclic aromatic, and pyridine is heterocyclic.
Why go through all this? Because reactivity follows class and functional group, not the individual molecule. Classify correctly and you can predict the chemistry before writing a single reaction.

segments_hinglish.text: किसी भी reaction को हाथ लगाने से पहले, आप classify करते हो। और classification का एक fixed order है: पहले carbon skeleton तय करो, फिर functional group।
Question one बस इतना: carbon framework एक open chain है, या closed ring? Open chain मतलब acyclic; ring मतलब cyclic।
Board पर पूरा family tree है। इसे ऊपर से नीचे follow करो और हर organic compound को exactly एक घर मिल जाता है।
अगर cyclic है, तो question two पूछो। क्या ring में सिर्फ़ carbon है, जो इसे carbocyclic बनाता है, या इसमें कोई non-carbon atom है, जो इसे heterocyclic बनाता है?
अगर carbocyclic है, तो एक और question। ये aromatic है, यानी benzene-type ring, या alicyclic, यानी एक ordinary non-aromatic ring?
<curious>Priority ध्यान से देखो। अगर ring में heteroatom है, तो वो पहले heterocyclic है, चाहे वो aromatic भी हो। Pyridine classic case है: heterocyclic aromatic को beat करता है।
कुछ anchors पकड़ लो: butane acyclic है, cyclohexane एक carbocyclic alicyclic ring है, benzene carbocyclic aromatic है, और pyridine heterocyclic है।
ये सब क्यों? क्योंकि reactivity class और functional group को follow करती है, individual molecule को नहीं। सही classify करो और आप एक भी reaction लिखे बिना chemistry predict कर सकते हो।

board_content.text: Functional group = the reactive heart
The atom or group that defines a molecule's characteristic chemistry.
Common: -OH alcohol · -CHO aldehyde · C=O ketone · -COOH acid · -NH2 amine · -C≡N nitrile · -X haloalkane.
Homologous series = a chemical family
Same functional group + one general formula; successive members differ by one -CH2- unit.
Boiling point rises steadily up a series; chemistry stays similar (same group).

segments_english.text: Within any molecule there's a reactive heart, and we call it the functional group.
Formally, the functional group is the atom or group of atoms that defines a molecule's characteristic chemistry. It's the part that actually reacts.

The common ones to know by sight: hydroxyl gives alcohols, C H O gives aldehydes, a carbonyl gives ketones, C O O H gives carboxylic acids, N H two gives amines, the cyano group gives nitriles, and a halogen gives haloalkanes.
Now group molecules into families. A homologous series is a chemical family, and its members are called homologues.
The members all share one functional group and one general formula, and each successive member differs from the last by exactly one C H two unit.
For the alkanes, that general formula is C n H two n plus two.
For the alkenes, with one double bond, it's C n H two n.
And for the alkynes, with a triple bond, it's C n H two n minus two.

<curious>The payoff is prediction. As you climb a series, boiling point rises steadily, while the chemistry stays similar because the functional group never changes. Know one member well and you can interpolate the rest.

segments_hinglish.text: किसी भी molecule के अंदर एक reactive heart होता है, और उसे हम functional group कहते हैं।
Formally, functional group वो atom या group of atoms है जो molecule की characteristic chemistry define करता है। यही हिस्सा असल में react करता है।
देखते ही पहचानने वाले common groups: hydroxyl से alcohols, C H O से aldehydes, carbonyl से ketones, C O O H से carboxylic acids, N H two से amines, cyano group से nitriles, और halogen से haloalkanes।
अब molecules को families में group करो। एक homologous series एक chemical family है, और इसके members को homologues कहते हैं।
सारे members एक ही functional group और एक general formula share करते हैं, और हर अगला member पिछले से exactly एक C H two unit से अलग होता है।
Alkanes के लिए वो general formula है C n H two n plus two।
Alkenes के लिए, एक double bond के साथ, ये है C n H two n।
और alkynes के लिए, एक triple bond के साथ, ये है C n H two n minus two।

<curious>फ़ायदा है prediction। जैसे-जैसे आप series में ऊपर चढ़ते हो, boiling point steadily बढ़ती है, जबकि chemistry similar रहती है क्योंकि functional group कभी नहीं बदलता। एक member अच्छे से जानो और बाक़ी interpolate कर सकते हो।

Task: write the condensed and bond-line formulae of 2-methylbutane.
Skeleton: a four-carbon main chain with a methyl branch on carbon 2.
Condensed: CH3CH(CH3)CH2CH3.

board_content.text: No H's, no C labels drawn — vertices and ends carry them silently.
Board habit: state the longest chain first, then attach branches — you never lose a carbon.
Check: 4 chain C + 1 branch C = 5 carbons = butane (4) + a 2-methyl branch.

segments_english.text: Let's put the drawing rules to work on a board-level question about a molecule called two-methylbutane.
The task is straightforward: write both the condensed formula and the bond-line formula for two-methylbutane.
First read the name into a skeleton. Butane gives a four-carbon main chain, and two-methyl attaches a one-carbon methyl branch onto carbon two.
Condensing it, we write C H three, then C H carrying a C H three in brackets, then C H two, then C H three.
Now the bond-line, on the board. A four-vertex zig-zag is the main chain, and a single extra line rising off the second vertex is the methyl branch.
<whisper>And notice what's missing. No hydrogens, no letter C anywhere. Every vertex and every free end silently carries a carbon with its hydrogens filled in.
The board habit that saves you: always state the longest chain first, then attach the branches. Do it in that order and you never accidentally drop a carbon.
Quick check. Four carbons in the chain plus one in the branch is five carbons total, which matches butane, that's four, plus a two-methyl branch. It's consistent.

segments_hinglish.text: चलो drawing rules को एक board-level question पर लगाते हैं, एक molecule two-methylbutane पर।
Task सीधा है: two-methylbutane का condensed formula और bond-line formula दोनों लिखो।
पहले name को skeleton में पढ़ो। Butane एक four-carbon main chain देता है, और two-methyl एक one-carbon methyl branch carbon two पर लगाता है।
इसे condense करके, हम लिखते हैं C H three, फिर C H जिसके साथ brackets में C H three, फिर C H two, फिर C H three।
अब bond-line, board पर। एक four-vertex zig-zag main chain है, और दूसरे vertex से ऊपर उठती एक extra line methyl branch है।
<whisper>और देखो क्या missing है। कोई hydrogens नहीं, कहीं भी letter C नहीं। हर vertex और हर free end चुपचाप एक carbon रखता है जिसके hydrogens भर दिए गए हैं।
वो board habit जो आपको बचाती है: हमेशा पहले longest chain बताओ, फिर branches लगाओ। इसी order में करो और आप कभी गलती से एक carbon नहीं छोड़ोगे।
Quick check। Chain में चार carbons plus branch में एक, total पाँच carbons, जो butane से match करता है, यानी चार, plus एक two-methyl branch। Consistent है।

board_content.text: Worked example — classify three rings (N E E T)
Classify: pyridine, cyclohexane, naphthalene.
Pyridine: six-membered ring with one nitrogen → heterocyclic (and aromatic).
Cyclohexane: six-carbon ring, no double bonds → carbocyclic, alicyclic.
Naphthalene: fused all-carbon benzene rings → carbocyclic, aromatic (benzenoid).
Trap: calling pyridine 'aromatic carbocyclic.' The N makes it heterocyclic — that wins.
Follow the tree: ring? → carbon-only or heteroatom? → then aromatic vs alicyclic.
One nitrogen reroutes the whole classification — heteroatom is checked before aromaticity.

segments_english.text: This is a classic N E E T speed trap. Three ring compounds, classify each fully and fast.
Our three are pyridine, cyclohexane, and naphthalene. We'll walk each down the family tree.
Pyridine is a six-membered ring, but one of those ring atoms is a nitrogen. A heteroatom in the ring makes it heterocyclic, and it happens to be aromatic too.
Cyclohexane is a six-membered ring of only carbon with no double bonds. Only carbon means carbocyclic, and no aromatic system means alicyclic.
Naphthalene is two fused benzene rings, all carbon. All carbon keeps it carbocyclic, and the benzene systems make it aromatic, the benzenoid type.

<curious>Here's the trap the paper is hoping you fall into: labelling pyridine aromatic carbocyclic. Yes it's aromatic, but that ring nitrogen forces heterocyclic, and heteroatom classification takes precedence.
So follow the tree in order. Is it a ring? Then is it carbon-only or does it hold a heteroatom? Only after that do you ask aromatic versus alicyclic.
That single nitrogen reroutes the entire classification. Always check for a heteroatom before you check for aromaticity.

segments_hinglish.text: ये एक classic N E E T speed trap है। तीन ring compounds, हर एक को fully और fast classify करो।
हमारे तीन हैं pyridine, cyclohexane, और naphthalene। हम हर एक को family tree पर चलाएँगे।
Pyridine एक six-membered ring है, पर उन ring atoms में से एक nitrogen है। Ring में heteroatom इसे heterocyclic बनाता है, और साथ में ये aromatic भी है।
Cyclohexane सिर्फ़ carbon का एक six-membered ring है जिसमें कोई double bonds नहीं। सिर्फ़ carbon मतलब carbocyclic, और कोई aromatic system नहीं मतलब alicyclic।
Naphthalene दो fused benzene rings हैं, पूरा carbon। पूरा carbon इसे carbocyclic रखता है, और benzene systems इसे aromatic बनाते हैं, benzenoid type।

<curious>यहाँ वो trap है जिसमें paper चाहता है आप गिरो: pyridine को aromatic carbocyclic कहना। हाँ ये aromatic है, पर वो ring nitrogen heterocyclic force करता है, और heteroatom classification को precedence मिलती है।
तो tree को order में follow करो। ये ring है? फिर ये सिर्फ़ carbon है या इसमें heteroatom है? उसके बाद ही aromatic versus alicyclic पूछो।
वो एक अकेला nitrogen पूरी classification को reroute कर देता है। Aromaticity check करने से पहले हमेशा heteroatom check करो।

title: Worked example — a ketone family (JEE Main)

board_content.text: Worked example — a ketone family (J E E Main)
Given CnH2nO, reacts as a ketone. Find: group, series formula, next two homologues.
Functional group: carbonyl C=O flanked by two carbons → a ketone.
Smallest ketone needs C=O between two carbons → propanone, C3H6O.
Next homologues (+CH2 each): butanone C4H8O, then pentan-2-one C5H10O.
A ketone can't be smaller than propanone — the carbonyl must sit between two carbons.
One reasoning chain links general formula + functional group + the +CH2 rule.

segments_english.text: Now a J E E Main family question that stitches several ideas together.

We're given a compound with general formula C n H two n O that reacts as a ketone. We must name the functional group, give the series formula, and write the next two homologues of the simplest ketone.
The functional group first. A ketone is a carbonyl, C double bond O, flanked on both sides by carbon atoms.
The general formula for the whole ketone series is C n H two n O, which matches exactly what we were given, so we're on the right track.
Now the simplest member. Because the carbonyl must sit between two carbons, the smallest possible ketone is propanone, C three H six O, with three carbons.
Climb the ladder by adding one C H two each time. After propanone comes butanone, C four H eight O, and then pentan-two-one, C five H ten O.
<curious>Notice why we couldn't start smaller. A ketone's carbonyl must be sandwiched between two carbons, so anything below three carbons simply isn't a ketone.
In one chain of reasoning you connected a general formula, a functional group, and the plus C H two homologue rule. That's exactly the family question J E E Main loves to set.

segments_hinglish.text: अब एक J E E Main family question जो कई ideas को एक साथ जोड़ता है।

हमें एक compound दिया है general formula C n H two n O के साथ जो ketone की तरह react करता है। हमें functional group name करना है, series formula देना है, और simplest ketone के अगले दो homologues लिखने हैं।
पहले functional group। एक ketone एक carbonyl है, C double bond O, जिसके दोनों तरफ़ carbon atoms हैं।
पूरी ketone series का general formula है C n H two n O, जो बिलकुल वही है जो हमें दिया गया, तो हम सही track पर हैं।
अब simplest member। क्योंकि carbonyl को दो carbons के बीच होना ज़रूरी है, सबसे छोटा possible ketone है propanone, C three H six O, तीन carbons के साथ।
हर बार एक C H two जोड़कर ladder चढ़ो। Propanone के बाद आता है butanone, C four H eight O, और फिर pentan-two-one, C five H ten O।
<curious>ध्यान दो हम इससे छोटा क्यों नहीं शुरू कर सके। Ketone का carbonyl दो carbons के बीच होना ही चाहिए, तो तीन carbons से नीचे कुछ भी ketone है ही नहीं।
एक ही chain of reasoning में आपने general formula, functional group, और plus C H two homologue rule को जोड़ा। यही वो family question है जो J E E Main को बहुत पसंद है।

title: Worked example — read a bond-line ring (JEE Advanced)

board_content.text: Worked example — read a bond-line ring (J E E Advanced)

board_content.caption: Six-carbon ring: one C=C, one -OH

board_content.text: Six ring vertices = six carbons. One C=C inside the ring; one carbon carries -OH.
Fill H by tetravalence: two sp2 C (one bears OH), four sp3 C carry 2 H each.
Classification: cyclic → carbocyclic → alicyclic, bearing an alcohol group. A cyclohexenol.
One C=C in a ring is NOT aromatic. Aromatic needs a fully conjugated, planar, (4n+2) pi ring.
Rigour: 'alicyclic vs aromatic' is the exact discrimination Advanced papers exploit.

segments_english.text: Finally a J E E Advanced problem that tests whether you can truly read a bond-line ring, not just draw one.
On the board is a six-vertex ring with one double bond between two adjacent ring carbons, and an O H drawn on one vertex.
Start counting. Six vertices means six ring carbons. There's one carbon-carbon double bond inside the ring, and one of the carbons also carries a hydroxyl group.

Now fill hydrogens by tetravalence. The two double-bonded carbons are s p two; one of them bears the O H so carries no extra hydrogen, the other carries one. The four remaining s p three carbons carry two hydrogens each.
Add it all up and the molecular formula comes out as C six H ten O.
For classification: it's cyclic, the ring is all carbon so carbocyclic, and despite that one double bond it is non-aromatic, so alicyclic, carrying an alcohol group. It's a cyclohexenol.

<whisper>Here's the rigour point Advanced papers exploit. A single carbon-carbon double bond in a ring does not make it aromatic. Aromaticity demands a fully conjugated, planar ring with four n plus two pi electrons.
So the discrimination they're testing is alicyclic versus aromatic. One lonely double bond is nowhere near enough for aromaticity, and knowing that difference is the whole mark.

segments_hinglish.text: आख़िर में एक J E E Advanced problem जो test करता है कि आप सच में एक bond-line ring पढ़ सकते हो, सिर्फ़ draw नहीं।
Board पर एक six-vertex ring है जिसमें दो adjacent ring carbons के बीच एक double bond है, और एक vertex पर एक O H बना है।
गिनना शुरू करो। छह vertices मतलब छह ring carbons। Ring के अंदर एक carbon-carbon double bond है, और एक carbon के साथ एक hydroxyl group भी है।
अब tetravalence से hydrogens भरो। दोनों double-bonded carbons s p two हैं; उनमें से एक O H रखता है तो कोई extra hydrogen नहीं, दूसरा एक रखता है। बाक़ी चार s p three carbons दो-दो hydrogens रखते हैं।
सब जोड़ो और molecular formula निकलता है C six H ten O।
Classification के लिए: ये cyclic है, ring पूरा carbon है तो carbocyclic, और उस एक double bond के बावजूद ये non-aromatic है, यानी alicyclic, एक alcohol group के साथ। ये एक cyclohexenol है।

<whisper>यहाँ वो rigour point है जिसे Advanced papers exploit करते हैं। Ring में एक अकेला carbon-carbon double bond इसे aromatic नहीं बनाता। Aromaticity माँगती है एक fully conjugated, planar ring जिसमें four n plus two pi electrons हों।
तो जो discrimination वो test कर रहे हैं वो है alicyclic versus aromatic। एक अकेला double bond aromaticity के आस-पास भी नहीं, और यही difference जानना पूरा mark है।

board_content.text: Pitfalls & pro-tips — Foundations
Pitfall 1: forgetting vertex = carbon. Every corner and free end is a carbon with H's filled in.
Pitfall 2: hiding heteroatoms. O, N, halogens — and their attached H's — are always drawn.
Pitfall 3: heteroatom beats aromatic. Pyridine is heterocyclic first, aromatic second.
Pitfall 4: CH2 is the homologous increment — and one lone ring double bond is NOT aromatic.
Pro-tip (speed): count vertices/ends for C, then fill H to reach four bonds on each.
Never count hydrogens one at a time across the whole structure — fill them by tetravalence.
Master these four and organic classification stops costing you silent marks.

segments_english.text: Let's close the foundations with the traps that quietly cost marks, and the shortcuts that save time.
Pitfall one, the big one: forgetting that a vertex is a carbon. Every unlabelled corner and every free end in a bond-line drawing is a carbon, with its hydrogens filled in automatically.
Pitfall two: hiding heteroatoms. Oxygen, nitrogen and the halogens, along with any hydrogens attached to them, are always drawn explicitly. Only the carbon-hydrogen bonds get suppressed.
Pitfall three, and mark it in red: heteroatom beats aromatic. When a ring holds a non-carbon atom, it is heterocyclic first and aromatic only second. Pyridine, once more, is the case to remember.
Pitfall four is really two habits. C H two is the homologous increment between family members, and a single lonely double bond inside a ring does not make that ring aromatic.
<excited>Now the speed pro-tip. To pull a molecular formula off a bond-line drawing fast, first count all the vertices and line-ends for your carbons.
Then, for hydrogens, just give each carbon exactly enough hydrogen to reach four bonds. Never crawl across the structure counting hydrogens one by one.
Master these four traps and this speed habit, and the whole of organic classification stops quietly bleeding you marks.

segments_hinglish.text: चलो foundations को उन traps के साथ बंद करते हैं जो चुपचाप marks खाते हैं, और उन shortcuts के साथ जो time बचाते हैं।
Pitfall one, सबसे बड़ी: भूल जाना कि vertex एक carbon है। Bond-line drawing में हर unlabelled corner और हर free end एक carbon है, जिसके hydrogens अपने आप भर जाते हैं।
Pitfall two: heteroatoms छुपाना। Oxygen, nitrogen और halogens, उनसे जुड़े किसी भी hydrogen के साथ, हमेशा explicitly draw होते हैं। सिर्फ़ carbon-hydrogen bonds ही suppress होते हैं।

Pitfall three, और इसे red में mark कर लो: heteroatom aromatic को beat करता है। जब ring में कोई non-carbon atom हो, तो वो पहले heterocyclic है और aromatic बाद में। Pyridine, एक बार फिर, याद रखने वाला case है।
Pitfall four असल में दो habits हैं। C H two family members के बीच homologous increment है, और ring के अंदर एक अकेला double bond उस ring को aromatic नहीं बनाता।
<excited>अब speed pro-tip। Bond-line drawing से molecular formula जल्दी निकालने के लिए, पहले सारे vertices और line-ends गिनकर अपने carbons निकालो।
फिर, hydrogens के लिए, हर carbon को बस इतना hydrogen दो कि चार bonds पूरे हो जाएँ। कभी पूरी structure पर एक-एक hydrogen गिनते मत घूमो।
इन चार traps और इस speed habit को master कर लो, और पूरी organic classification चुपचाप आपके marks बहाना बंद कर देगी।

title: Hybridization — why carbon won't behave on paper

board_content.text: Hybridization — why carbon won't behave 'on paper'
On paper: carbon has 2 electrons in a spherical 2s and 2 in dumbbell 2p orbitals.
Predicted: methane's C-H bonds should differ. Observed: all four identical, tetrahedral.
Nature's fix: mix the orbitals. Empty them out and repack into identical hybrids.
Sabziwala repack: 1 big bag onions (s) + 3 equal bags potatoes (p) → 4 identical mixed bags.
1s+3p → four sp3.  1s+2p → three sp2 (1 pure p left).  1s+1p → two sp (2 pure p left).
The leftover pure p orbitals form the pi bonds of double and triple bonds.
Rule of thumb: only single bonds → sp3; one double bond → sp2; triple / two doubles → sp.
Shortcut works because carbon has no lone pairs — N, O, charged C need lone-pair counting.

segments_english.text: Let's tackle hybridization, and the honest way in is to admit that carbon refuses to behave the way a naive picture predicts.
On paper, a carbon atom has two electrons sitting in a spherical two s orbital and two more in dumbbell-shaped two p orbitals.

If carbon used those orbitals as they are, methane's four carbon-hydrogen bonds would come in two different flavours and lengths. But experiment is blunt: all four bonds are identical, pointing to the corners of a perfect tetrahedron.
Nature resolves the contradiction by mixing. It empties the s and p orbitals and repacks them into a set of identical hybrid orbitals.

<curious>Picture a sabziwala with one large five kilogram bag of onions, the s orbital, and three identical one kilogram bags of potatoes, the p orbitals. A customer wants four equal mixed bags. The only fair solution is to empty everything and repack into four identical blends.

Mix one s with three p and you get four equal s p three orbitals. Mix one s with two p and you get three s p two, with one pure p left over. Mix one s with one p and you get two s p, with two pure p left over.
Those leftover pure p orbitals are exactly what form the second and third bonds of double and triple bonds, the pi bonds.
So the rule of thumb writes itself. A carbon making only single bonds is s p three. One double bond makes it s p two. A triple bond, or two cumulated double bonds, makes it s p.

One caution. This count-the-bonds shortcut works so cleanly for carbon precisely because carbon in stable molecules carries no lone pairs. The moment you move to nitrogen, oxygen, or a charged carbon, you must count lone pairs too.

segments_hinglish.text: चलो hybridization पकड़ते हैं, और इसमें घुसने का honest तरीक़ा है ये मानना कि carbon उस तरह behave नहीं करता जैसा naive picture predict करती है।
On paper, एक carbon atom के दो electrons एक spherical two s orbital में बैठते हैं और दो और dumbbell-shaped two p orbitals में।

अगर carbon इन orbitals को जैसे हैं वैसे use करता, तो methane के चार carbon-hydrogen bonds दो अलग flavours और lengths के होते। पर experiment साफ़ कहता है: चारों bonds identical हैं, एक perfect tetrahedron के corners की तरफ़।
Nature इस contradiction को mixing से हल करती है। ये s और p orbitals को खाली करके उन्हें identical hybrid orbitals के set में repack कर देती है।

<curious>एक सब्ज़ीवाला सोचो जिसके पास एक बड़ा पाँच किलो का onions का bag है, यानी s orbital, और तीन identical एक किलो के potatoes के bags, यानी p orbitals। Customer को चार बराबर mixed bags चाहिए। एकमात्र fair solution है सब खाली करके चार identical blends में repack करना।

एक s को तीन p के साथ mix करो और चार बराबर s p three orbitals मिलते हैं। एक s को दो p के साथ mix करो और तीन s p two मिलते हैं, एक pure p बचता है। एक s को एक p के साथ mix करो और दो s p मिलते हैं, दो pure p बचते हैं।
वही बचे हुए pure p orbitals double और triple bonds के दूसरे और तीसरे bonds बनाते हैं, यानी pi bonds।
तो rule of thumb ख़ुद बन जाता है। सिर्फ़ single bonds बनाने वाला carbon s p three है। एक double bond इसे s p two बनाता है। एक triple bond, या दो cumulated double bonds, इसे s p बनाते हैं।

एक caution। ये count-the-bonds shortcut carbon के लिए इतना clean काम करता है क्योंकि stable molecules में carbon के कोई lone pairs नहीं होते। जैसे ही आप nitrogen, oxygen, या charged carbon पर जाते हो, आपको lone pairs भी गिनने पड़ते हैं।

Higher %s-character = electrons held closer to the nucleus. This drives every trend below.
Bond length rises: sp C-H (shortest) → sp2 C-H → sp3 C-H (longest). More s = shorter, stronger.
Terminal C-H acidity: sp (most) → sp2 → sp3 (least). Same order for carbon electronegativity.

segments_english.text: With the why in hand, let's tabulate the three hybridizations of carbon and the geometry each one produces.
The board shows all three shapes together: the tetrahedron, the flat triangle, and the straight line.

An s p three carbon has four sigma bonds and no pi bonds. It's tetrahedral, with bond angles of one hundred nine point five degrees, twenty-five percent s character, and it's your typical alkane carbon.
An s p two carbon has three sigma bonds and one pi bond. It's trigonal planar, one hundred twenty degrees, thirty-three point three percent s character, the carbon of an alkene or a carbonyl.
An s p carbon has two sigma bonds and two pi bonds. It's linear, one hundred eighty degrees, fifty percent s character, the carbon of an alkyne or a nitrile.
<curious>Now the single idea that generates every trend. The more s character an orbital has, the closer the bonding electrons are held to the nucleus.
That controls bond length. More s character means a shorter, stronger sigma bond, so an s p carbon-hydrogen bond is shorter than an s p two, which is shorter than an s p three.
And it controls two more things. The terminal carbon-hydrogen bond is most acidic when the carbon is s p, and carbon's own electronegativity also runs highest for s p, then s p two, then s p three.

segments_hinglish.text: Why समझ लेने के बाद, चलो carbon की तीन hybridizations और हर एक जो geometry बनाती है उसे tabulate करते हैं।
Board तीनों shapes एक साथ दिखाता है: tetrahedron, flat triangle, और straight line।
एक s p three carbon के चार sigma bonds और कोई pi bond नहीं होता। ये tetrahedral है, bond angles one hundred nine point five degrees, twenty-five percent s character, और ये typical alkane carbon है।
एक s p two carbon के तीन sigma bonds और एक pi bond होता है। ये trigonal planar है, one hundred twenty degrees, thirty-three point three percent s character, alkene या carbonyl का carbon।
एक s p carbon के दो sigma bonds और दो pi bonds होते हैं। ये linear है, one hundred eighty degrees, fifty percent s character, alkyne या nitrile का carbon।
<curious>अब वो एक idea जो हर trend बनाता है। orbital में जितना ज़्यादा s character, bonding electrons उतने पास nucleus के पकड़े जाते हैं।
ये bond length control करता है। ज़्यादा s character मतलब छोटा, stronger sigma bond, तो एक s p carbon-hydrogen bond s p two से छोटा है, जो s p three से छोटा है।

और ये दो और चीज़ें control करता है। Terminal carbon-hydrogen bond सबसे ज़्यादा acidic तब है जब carbon s p हो, और carbon की अपनी electronegativity भी सबसे ज़्यादा s p के लिए, फिर s p two, फिर s p three चलती है।

title: Assign hybridization: just count sigma bonds

board_content.text: Assign hybridization: just count sigma bonds
Neutral C, no lone pair: count sigma bonds. Single = 1σ; double = 1σ+1π; triple = 1σ+2π.
The sigma-count is the steric number.
Steric number 4 → sp3;  3 → sp2;  2 → sp.
Pi bonds always use leftover unhybridized p — they NEVER raise the steric number.
Charged / heteroatom centres: add lone pairs. Carbocation 3σ+0lp → sp2; carbanion 3σ+1lp → sp3.
Propyne CH3-C≡CH: C1 has 4σ → sp3; C2 and C3 each 2σ → sp (linear region).
Never draw orbitals in an exam. Count sigma bonds (+ lone pairs) and read off the answer.

segments_english.text: Here's the procedure you'll actually use in an exam, and it takes about three seconds per carbon.
For a neutral carbon with no lone pair, simply count its sigma bonds. A single bond is one sigma. A double bond is one sigma plus one pi. A triple bond is one sigma plus two pi.
That sigma-count is what we call the steric number.
Then just read it off. Steric number four gives s p three, three gives s p two, and two gives s p.
<excited>Here is the beautiful reason this works. Pi bonds are always made from leftover unhybridized p orbitals, so a pi bond never adds to the steric number. You literally ignore the pi bonds.

For a charged centre or a heteroatom, add any lone pairs to the count. A carbocation carbon has three sigma bonds and no lone pair, so s p two. A carbanion carbon has three sigma bonds and one lone pair, so s p three.

Take propyne, C H three attached to a carbon triple bonded to C H. The methyl carbon has four sigma bonds, so s p three. The two triple-bonded carbons each have just two sigma bonds, so both are s p, which is why that region is perfectly linear.
So the exam habit is blunt: never draw orbitals. Count sigma bonds, add lone pairs if there's a charge or heteroatom, and read the answer straight off.

segments_hinglish.text: अब वो procedure जो आप सच में exam में use करोगे, और ये हर carbon पर लगभग तीन seconds लेता है।
एक neutral carbon के लिए जिसमें lone pair नहीं, बस उसके sigma bonds गिनो। एक single bond एक sigma है। एक double bond एक sigma plus एक pi। एक triple bond एक sigma plus दो pi।
वो sigma-count ही है जिसे हम steric number कहते हैं।
फिर बस पढ़ लो। Steric number four देता है s p three, three देता है s p two, और two देता है s p।
<excited>अब वो सुंदर वजह क्यों ये काम करता है। Pi bonds हमेशा बचे हुए unhybridized p orbitals से बनते हैं, तो एक pi bond कभी steric number में नहीं जुड़ता। आप literally pi bonds को ignore कर देते हो।

एक charged centre या heteroatom के लिए, count में lone pairs जोड़ो। एक carbocation carbon के तीन sigma bonds और कोई lone pair नहीं, तो s p two। एक carbanion carbon के तीन sigma bonds और एक lone pair, तो s p three।

Propyne लो, C H three एक carbon से जुड़ा जो C H से triple bonded है। Methyl carbon के चार sigma bonds, तो s p three। दोनों triple-bonded carbons के सिर्फ़ दो sigma bonds, तो दोनों s p, इसीलिए वो region perfectly linear है।
तो exam habit साफ़ है: कभी orbitals मत बनाओ। Sigma bonds गिनो, charge या heteroatom हो तो lone pairs जोड़ो, और जवाब सीधा पढ़ लो।

board_content.text: Nomenclature — chemistry's PIN-code system
Millions of compounds: common names can't scale. IUPAC = one name per structure, one structure per name.
An IUPAC name is a postal address written backwards: landmark → locality → lane → house number.

Roots: 1 meth · 2 eth · 3 prop · 4 but · 5 pent · 6 hex · 7 hept · 8 oct · 9 non · 10 dec.
Read the structure off the name; rebuild the name off the structure. Nothing is guessed.
Ties are broken by explicit rules — and those tie-breaks are exactly where exam marks are won and lost.

segments_english.text: Now the other half of this subtopic, naming. And naming is the single most reliable place to score in the whole chapter, so let's build the system properly.

There are millions of organic compounds, and common names like acetic acid could never scale to all of them. The I U P A C system fixes this: exactly one correct name per compound, and one structure per name.

<curious>Think of an I U P A C name as a postal address written backwards. You start from the most important landmark, the principal functional group, then give the locality, the parent chain, then the lane markers, the substituents, and finally the house numbers, the locants.
The board breaks a name into its slots so you can see the machinery, using three-hydroxybutanal as the example.

Reading left to right: the prefixes carry the substituents, the root gives the carbon count, the middle piece marks single, double or triple bonds as ane, ene or yne, and the suffix names the principal group.
Memorise the carbon-count roots once and for all: meth, eth, prop, but for one through four, then pent, hex, hept, oct, non, dec for five through ten.
The whole point is reversibility. You can read the structure straight off a correct name, and rebuild the name straight off a structure. Nothing is ever guessed.
One warning to carry forward. When two naming choices tie, I U P A C has explicit tie-breakers, and those tie-breaks are exactly where exam marks are won and lost.

segments_hinglish.text: अब इस subtopic का दूसरा हिस्सा, naming। और naming पूरे chapter में score करने की सबसे reliable जगह है, तो चलो system को ठीक से बनाते हैं।

Millions of organic compounds हैं, और acetic acid जैसे common names इन सबके लिए scale नहीं कर सकते। I U P A C system इसे fix करता है: हर compound का exactly एक correct name, और हर name की एक structure।

<curious>एक I U P A C name को उल्टा लिखा हुआ postal address समझो। आप सबसे important landmark से शुरू करते हो, यानी principal functional group, फिर locality देते हो, parent chain, फिर lane markers, substituents, और आख़िर में house numbers, locants।
Board एक name को उसके slots में तोड़ता है ताकि आप machinery देख सको, three-hydroxybutanal को example बनाकर।

बाएँ से दाएँ पढ़ते हुए: prefixes substituents रखते हैं, root carbon count देता है, बीच का piece single, double या triple bonds को ane, ene या yne से mark करता है, और suffix principal group को name करता है।
Carbon-count roots एक बार में हमेशा के लिए याद कर लो: meth, eth, prop, but एक से चार के लिए, फिर pent, hex, hept, oct, non, dec पाँच से दस के लिए।
पूरी बात reversibility की है। आप एक correct name से सीधा structure पढ़ सकते हो, और एक structure से सीधा name बना सकते हो। कुछ भी guess नहीं किया जाता।
एक warning आगे के लिए। जब दो naming choices tie करती हैं, I U P A C के पास explicit tie-breakers हैं, और वही tie-breaks वो जगह हैं जहाँ exam marks जीते और हारे जाते हैं।

title: Building a name: lock the suffix first

board_content.text: Building a name: lock the suffix first
Seniority (high → low): COOH → SO3H → ester → amide → CN → CHO → C=O → OH → NH2.
Suffix / prefix: -COOH -oic acid / carboxy · -OH -ol / hydroxy · C=O -one / oxo · -NH2 -amine / amino.
Halogens, -NO2, alkyl and alkoxy are ALWAYS prefixes — never the principal group.
Step 1-2: pick principal group → suffix; select the longest chain that CONTAINS that group.
Step 3: number for the lowest locant to the principal group first.
Step 4-5: substituents as alphabetical prefixes; break ties by first point of difference — {2,3,6} beats {2,4,5}.
Alphabetize ignoring di/tri/tetra and sec-/tert-; but cyclo- and iso- DO count.

segments_english.text: So here is the build procedure, and the golden move is to lock the suffix before you touch anything else.

First, the seniority list that decides the suffix. Carboxylic acid outranks sulphonic acid, then come esters, amides, the nitrile group, the aldehyde, the ketone carbonyl, then hydroxyl, and finally the amino group at the bottom.

Each principal group has a suffix form and a demoted prefix form. Carboxylic acid is oic acid as a suffix or carboxy as a prefix. Hydroxyl is ol or hydroxy. The ketone carbonyl is one or oxo. The amino group is amine or amino.
<curious>And a hard rule to memorise: halogens, the nitro group, and alkyl or alkoxy groups are always prefixes. They can never be the principal group, no matter what else is in the molecule.
Now the steps. First identify the principal group using seniority, which fixes the suffix. Then select the parent chain as the longest continuous chain that actually contains that principal group.
Third, number the chain so the principal characteristic group gets the lowest possible locant first.

Fourth, name the substituents as prefixes in alphabetical order, each with its locant. If two numbering directions tie, break the tie by first point of difference: compare the locant sets term by term, and the set that is lower at the first difference wins. So two, three, six beats two, four, five.
One last subtlety when alphabetizing. Ignore the multiplying prefixes di, tri and tetra, and ignore sec and tert, but the prefixes cyclo and iso do count as letters.

segments_hinglish.text: तो ये रहा build procedure, और golden move है suffix को किसी और चीज़ को छूने से पहले lock कर लेना।

पहले वो seniority list जो suffix तय करती है। Carboxylic acid sulphonic acid को outrank करता है, फिर आते हैं esters, amides, nitrile group, aldehyde, ketone carbonyl, फिर hydroxyl, और आख़िर में amino group सबसे नीचे।

हर principal group का एक suffix form और एक demoted prefix form होता है। Carboxylic acid suffix में oic acid या prefix में carboxy। Hydroxyl ol या hydroxy। Ketone carbonyl one या oxo। Amino group amine या amino।
<curious>और एक hard rule याद कर लो: halogens, nitro group, और alkyl या alkoxy groups हमेशा prefixes होते हैं। ये कभी principal group नहीं बन सकते, molecule में चाहे और कुछ भी हो।
अब steps। पहले seniority से principal group पहचानो, जो suffix fix करता है। फिर parent chain चुनो, वो longest continuous chain जिसमें असल में वो principal group हो।
तीसरा, chain को इस तरह number करो कि principal characteristic group को पहले सबसे lowest possible locant मिले।

चौथा, substituents को alphabetical order में prefixes की तरह name करो, हर एक अपने locant के साथ। अगर दो numbering directions tie करें, तो tie को first point of difference से तोड़ो: locant sets को term by term compare करो, और जो set पहले difference पर lower है वो जीतता है। तो two, three, six two, four, five को beat करता है।
Alphabetize करते वक़्त एक आख़िरी subtlety। Multiplying prefixes di, tri और tetra को ignore करो, और sec और tert को ignore करो, पर prefixes cyclo और iso letters की तरह count होते हैं।

board_content.text: Seniority: -CHO (aldehyde) outranks -OH → suffix -al; the -OH is demoted to hydroxy-.
Chain 4 C incl. CHO → butanal. CHO is terminal → C1; OH on C3 → 3-hydroxybutanal.
Hybridization: C1 (CHO) sp2 · C2 (CH2) sp3 · C3 (CHOH) sp3 · C4 (CH3) sp3.
State the suffix group first, then demote the rest — this stops the classic 'naming it as an -ol' error.
Only C1 touches a double bond (C=O), so only C1 is sp2. Everything single-bonded is sp3.

segments_english.text: A board-level question that pairs naming with hybridization on the same molecule.
The compound is C H three, C H with an O H, C H two, C H O. We need its I U P A C name and the hybridization of every carbon.
There it is on the board in bond-line form: a four-carbon chain with an aldehyde at one end and a hydroxyl in the middle.
First lock the suffix. Two groups are present, the hydroxyl and the aldehyde. By seniority the aldehyde outranks the hydroxyl, so the suffix is al, and the hydroxyl is demoted to the prefix hydroxy.

The parent chain is four carbons including the aldehyde carbon, giving butanal. An aldehyde carbon is always terminal, so it must be carbon one, and the hydroxyl then sits on carbon three. The name is three-hydroxybutanal.
Now hybridization. Carbon one is the C H O, which has a carbon-oxygen double bond, so it's s p two. Carbons two, three and four make only single bonds, so all three are s p three.
<curious>Notice the habit that saves the marks. State the suffix group first, then demote everything below it. Do that and you'll never make the classic board error of naming this compound as an ol.
The clean summary: only carbon one touches a double bond, the carbonyl, so only carbon one is s p two. Everything single-bonded is s p three.

segments_hinglish.text: एक board-level question जो एक ही molecule पर naming और hybridization दोनों जोड़ता है।
Compound है C H three, C H जिसके साथ O H, C H two, C H O। हमें इसका I U P A C name और हर carbon की hybridization चाहिए।
वो रहा board पर bond-line form में: एक four-carbon chain जिसके एक सिरे पर aldehyde और बीच में एक hydroxyl।
पहले suffix lock करो। दो groups हैं, hydroxyl और aldehyde। Seniority से aldehyde hydroxyl को outrank करता है, तो suffix है al, और hydroxyl prefix hydroxy में demote हो जाता है।

Parent chain aldehyde carbon समेत चार carbons है, जो butanal देता है। Aldehyde carbon हमेशा terminal होता है, तो वो carbon one होना ही चाहिए, और hydroxyl फिर carbon three पर बैठता है। Name है three-hydroxybutanal।
अब hybridization। Carbon one वो C H O है, जिसमें carbon-oxygen double bond है, तो ये s p two। Carbons two, three और four सिर्फ़ single bonds बनाते हैं, तो तीनों s p three।
<curious>वो habit देखो जो marks बचाती है। पहले suffix group बताओ, फिर उसके नीचे सब कुछ demote करो। ऐसा करो और आप कभी वो classic board error नहीं करोगे कि इस compound को ol name कर दो।
Clean summary: सिर्फ़ carbon one एक double bond, carbonyl, को छूता है, तो सिर्फ़ carbon one s p two है। बाक़ी सब single-bonded s p three है।

board_content.text: Worked example — count sp2 carbons (N E E T)
In but-3-en-2-one (methyl vinyl ketone), CH2=CH-CO-CH3, how many carbons are sp2?
Speed method: scan for double bonds — every carbon touching a double bond is sp2.
C=C contributes two sp2 carbons; C=O contributes one more.
C4 (CH3) 4σ → sp3 · C3 (C=O) sp2 · C2 (=CH) sp2 · C1 (=CH2) sp2.
Answer: three sp2 carbons.
Trap: counting the two alkene carbons but forgetting the carbonyl carbon is ALSO sp2.
Mental check: every carbon touching a double bond — including C=O — is sp2.

segments_english.text: A quick N E E T speed trap now, the kind you must clear in seconds.
In but-three-en-two-one, also called methyl vinyl ketone, with structure C H two double bond C H, then C O, then C H three, how many carbons are s p two hybridized?
The speed method is to scan only for double bonds, because every carbon that touches a double bond is s p two.
The carbon-carbon double bond contributes two s p two carbons, and the carbon-oxygen double bond of the ketone contributes one more.

Going through them: carbon four is the methyl with four sigma bonds, so s p three. Carbon three is the carbonyl, s p two. Carbon two is a double-bonded C H, s p two. Carbon one is the double-bonded C H two, s p two.
So the answer is three s p two carbons.

<curious>And here is the trap the paper sets. Students count the two alkene carbons and then forget that the carbonyl carbon is also s p two. That carbonyl is the most-missed s p two centre in the whole exam.
So keep a mental check running: every carbon touching a double bond, and that includes the C double bond O, is s p two.

segments_hinglish.text: अब एक जल्दी N E E T speed trap, वो type जो आपको seconds में clear करना है।
But-three-en-two-one में, जिसे methyl vinyl ketone भी कहते हैं, structure C H two double bond C H, फिर C O, फिर C H three, कितने carbons s p two hybridized हैं?
Speed method है सिर्फ़ double bonds scan करना, क्योंकि हर carbon जो double bond को छूता है वो s p two है।
Carbon-carbon double bond दो s p two carbons देता है, और ketone का carbon-oxygen double bond एक और देता है।

एक-एक देखते हुए: carbon four वो methyl है चार sigma bonds के साथ, तो s p three। Carbon three carbonyl है, s p two। Carbon two एक double-bonded C H है, s p two। Carbon one double-bonded C H two है, s p two।
तो जवाब है तीन s p two carbons।

<curious>और यहाँ वो trap है जो paper लगाता है। Students दोनों alkene carbons गिन लेते हैं और फिर भूल जाते हैं कि carbonyl carbon भी s p two है। वो carbonyl पूरे exam में सबसे ज़्यादा miss होने वाला s p two centre है।
तो एक mental check चलाते रहो: हर carbon जो double bond को छूता है, और इसमें C double bond O भी शामिल है, s p two है।

board_content.text: Worked example — name + property (J E E Main)
Name CH2=CH-CH(CH3)-COOH and give the hybridization of C2.
Principal group -COOH → suffix -oic acid; its carbon is C1.
Longest chain through COOH = 4 C → butanoic acid backbone.
Double bond C3-C4 → but-3-enoic acid; methyl on C2 → 2-methyl. Name: 2-methylbut-3-enoic acid.
C2 bears methyl, H, C1, C3 — all single bonds → 4σ → sp3. (C1, C3, C4 are sp2.)
Seniority still anchors the numbering: COOH fixes C1 even though it 'demotes nothing' here.
Standard JEE Main move: seniority + longest chain through the group + lowest-locant + a hybridization count.

segments_english.text: Now the standard J E E Main pairing: name the compound and pull one property from it.
Name C H two double bond C H, then C H carrying a methyl, then C O O H, and give the hybridization of carbon two.
Lock the suffix first. The carboxylic acid is the principal group, so the suffix is oic acid, and its carbon becomes carbon one.
The longest chain running through that C O O H is four carbons, so the backbone is butanoic acid.

There's a double bond between carbons three and four, giving but-three-enoic acid, and a methyl branch sits on carbon two, giving the two-methyl prefix. Assembled, the name is two-methylbut-three-enoic acid.

For carbon two: it carries the methyl, a hydrogen, carbon one and carbon three, all through single bonds, so four sigma bonds, so s p three. For contrast, carbon one is s p two from the carbonyl, and carbons three and four are s p two from the double bond.

<curious>Note the quiet role of seniority here. Even though the carboxylic acid demotes nothing else in this molecule, it still fixes carbon one and anchors the whole numbering. Seniority earns its keep even when it looks idle.
This is the standard J E E Main move in one question: seniority to fix the suffix, longest chain through that group, lowest-locant numbering, and then a quick hybridization count on top.

segments_hinglish.text: अब standard J E E Main pairing: compound को name करो और उसमें से एक property निकालो।
Name करो C H two double bond C H, फिर C H जिसके साथ एक methyl, फिर C O O H, और carbon two की hybridization दो।
पहले suffix lock करो। Carboxylic acid principal group है, तो suffix है oic acid, और इसका carbon carbon one बन जाता है।
उस C O O H से गुज़रती longest chain चार carbons है, तो backbone है butanoic acid।

Carbons three और four के बीच एक double bond है, जो but-three-enoic acid देता है, और carbon two पर एक methyl branch है, जो two-methyl prefix देता है। Assemble करने पर name है two-methylbut-three-enoic acid।

Carbon two के लिए: ये methyl, एक hydrogen, carbon one और carbon three रखता है, सब single bonds से, तो चार sigma bonds, तो s p three। Contrast के लिए, carbon one carbonyl से s p two है, और carbons three और four double bond से s p two हैं।

<curious>यहाँ seniority का चुपचाप role देखो। भले ही carboxylic acid इस molecule में और कुछ demote नहीं करता, फिर भी ये carbon one fix करता है और पूरी numbering को anchor करता है। Seniority तब भी काम की है जब वो idle दिखती है।
ये एक ही question में standard J E E Main move है: suffix fix करने के लिए seniority, उस group से गुज़रती longest chain, lowest-locant numbering, और ऊपर से एक quick hybridization count।

title: Worked example — the alkyne trap (JEE Advanced)

board_content.text: Worked example — the alkyne trap (J E E Advanced)
Compound HC≡C-CH(OH)-COOH: name it, hybridize every carbon, explain the C3-C4 geometry.

board_content.text: Principal group -COOH outranks -OH → suffix -oic acid, C of COOH is C1; OH becomes 2-hydroxy-.
Chain 4 C; triple bond C3-C4 → but-3-ynoic acid. Name: 2-hydroxybut-3-ynoic acid.
Hybridization: C1 (COOH) sp2 · C2 (CHOH) sp3 · C3 (≡C) sp · C4 (≡CH) sp.
Geometry C3-C4: both sp, collinear at 180°; C≡C = one sigma + two perpendicular pi bonds, cylindrically symmetric.
Trap: numbering from the alkyne end to get 'but-1-ynoic acid'. -COOH seniority forces C1 onto the acid carbon.

segments_english.text: Finally the J E E Advanced version, and it hides a very specific trap in the numbering.
The compound is H C triple bond C, then C H with an O H, then C O O H. We must name it, hybridize every carbon, and explain the geometry around carbons three and four.
On the board you can see the shape: a straight, linear triple-bonded end, and the carboxylic acid at the other end.
Lock the suffix. The carboxylic acid outranks the hydroxyl, so the suffix is oic acid and the acid carbon is carbon one; the hydroxyl becomes the prefix two-hydroxy.
The parent chain is four carbons, so a but-something-oic acid, and the triple bond sits between carbons three and four, giving but-three-ynoic acid. The full name is two-hydroxybut-three-ynoic acid.
Hybridization straight down the chain: carbon one, the C O O H, is s p two. Carbon two, the C H O H, is s p three. Carbons three and four are both s p, because each has only two sigma bonds.

Now the geometry. Both s p carbons are collinear with their neighbours, so the hydrogen, carbon four, carbon three, and carbon two all lie on one straight line at one hundred eighty degrees. The triple bond is one sigma bond plus two mutually perpendicular pi bonds, giving a cylindrically symmetric electron cloud around the C triple bond C axis.

<whisper>And here's the exact trap. Advanced tempts you to number from the alkyne end and call it but-one-ynoic acid. But the seniority of the carboxylic acid forces carbon one onto the acid carbon, no matter where the triple bond sits.

segments_hinglish.text: आख़िर में J E E Advanced version, और ये numbering में एक बहुत specific trap छुपाता है।
Compound है H C triple bond C, फिर C H जिसके साथ O H, फिर C O O H। हमें इसे name करना है, हर carbon को hybridize करना है, और carbons three और four के आस-पास की geometry explain करनी है।
Board पर आप shape देख सकते हो: एक सीधा, linear triple-bonded सिरा, और दूसरे सिरे पर carboxylic acid।
Suffix lock करो। Carboxylic acid hydroxyl को outrank करता है, तो suffix है oic acid और acid carbon carbon one है; hydroxyl prefix two-hydroxy बन जाता है।
Parent chain चार carbons है, तो एक but-something-oic acid, और triple bond carbons three और four के बीच है, जो but-three-ynoic acid देता है। पूरा name है two-hydroxybut-three-ynoic acid।
Chain के साथ सीधे hybridization: carbon one, C O O H, s p two है। Carbon two, C H O H, s p three है। Carbons three और four दोनों s p हैं, क्योंकि हर एक के सिर्फ़ दो sigma bonds हैं।

अब geometry। दोनों s p carbons अपने neighbours के साथ collinear हैं, तो hydrogen, carbon four, carbon three, और carbon two सब एक सीधी line पर one hundred eighty degrees पर हैं। Triple bond एक sigma bond plus दो mutually perpendicular pi bonds है, जो C triple bond C axis के around एक cylindrically symmetric electron cloud देता है।

<whisper>और यहाँ वो exact trap है। Advanced आपको लुभाता है कि alkyne सिरे से number करके इसे but-one-ynoic acid कहो। पर carboxylic acid की seniority carbon one को acid carbon पर force करती है, triple bond चाहे कहीं भी हो।

board_content.text: Pitfalls & pro-tips — Hybridization & Naming
Pitfall 1 (ORG-NOM-PRINCIPAL-GROUP): naming the wrong group as suffix. Run seniority first; demote the rest.
Pitfall 2 (ORG-NOM-CHAIN-SELECT): missing the longest chain — it may bend through a 'branch'. Trace every path.
Pitfall 3 (ORG-NOM-LOCANT-TIEBREAK): tie-break is first point of difference, NOT lowest sum. {2,7,8} beats {3,4,8}.
Pitfall 4 (ORG-HYB-CARBONYL-SP2): the carbonyl carbon is sp2 — the most-forgotten centre.
Pitfall 5 (ORG-HYB-CHARGED-CENTRE): don't apply the neutral shortcut blindly to a carbocation/carbanion — add lone pairs.
Pro-tip (hybridization): never draw orbitals — sigma-count (+ lone pairs) = 4,3,2 → sp3, sp2, sp.
Pro-tip (naming): lock the suffix before the chain — it fixes the parent AND C1 and prevents ~80% of locant errors.

segments_english.text: Let's close this subtopic with the traps that cost the most marks and the two habits that save the most time.

Pitfall one, tagged principal group. Beginners see both a carboxylic acid and a hydroxyl and name the compound as an ol. Always run the seniority list first, and demote everything below the winner to a prefix.
Pitfall two, chain selection. The longest chain does not have to be the one drawn horizontally. It may bend through what looks like a branch, so trace every path before you commit.

Pitfall three, and this one is worth red ink. The lowest-locant tie-break is decided by first point of difference, not by the smallest sum. The set two, seven, eight actually beats three, four, eight, even though its sum is larger, because it's lower at the very first term.
Pitfall four, the carbonyl. That carbonyl carbon is s p two, and it is the single most commonly forgotten s p two centre in exams.
Pitfall five, charged centres. Don't apply the neutral count-the-bonds shortcut blindly to a carbocation or carbanion. Add the lone pairs, and the answer shifts.

<excited>Now the two pro-tips. For hybridization, never draw orbitals. Just count sigma bonds, add lone pairs if needed, and a count of four, three or two reads straight off as s p three, s p two, or s p.
And for naming, lock the suffix before you touch the chain. That one move fixes both the parent chain and carbon one at the same time, and it prevents around eighty percent of all locant errors.

segments_hinglish.text: चलो इस subtopic को उन traps के साथ बंद करते हैं जो सबसे ज़्यादा marks खाते हैं और उन दो habits के साथ जो सबसे ज़्यादा time बचाती हैं।

Pitfall one, principal group tag वाली। Beginners एक carboxylic acid और एक hydroxyl दोनों देखते हैं और compound को ol name कर देते हैं। हमेशा पहले seniority list चलाओ, और winner के नीचे सब कुछ prefix में demote करो।
Pitfall two, chain selection। Longest chain को horizontal draw की गई chain होना ज़रूरी नहीं। ये उस चीज़ से मुड़ सकती है जो branch दिखती है, तो commit करने से पहले हर path trace करो।

Pitfall three, और ये red ink के लायक़ है। Lowest-locant tie-break first point of difference से तय होता है, smallest sum से नहीं। Set two, seven, eight असल में three, four, eight को beat करता है, भले उसका sum बड़ा हो, क्योंकि वो पहले ही term पर lower है।
Pitfall four, carbonyl। वो carbonyl carbon s p two है, और ये exams में सबसे ज़्यादा भूला जाने वाला अकेला s p two centre है।
Pitfall five, charged centres। Neutral count-the-bonds shortcut को carbocation या carbanion पर आँख बंद करके मत लगाओ। Lone pairs जोड़ो, और जवाब बदल जाता है।
<excited>अब दो pro-tips। Hybridization के लिए, कभी orbitals मत बनाओ। बस sigma bonds गिनो, ज़रूरत हो तो lone pairs जोड़ो, और चार, तीन या दो का count सीधा s p three, s p two, या s p पढ़ लो।
और naming के लिए, chain छूने से पहले suffix lock करो। वो एक move एक साथ parent chain और carbon one दोनों fix करता है, और लगभग अस्सी percent locant errors रोकता है।

board_content.text: Isomers — same formula, different compound
Two people can share the same ID data yet be different individuals. Isomers are molecules in that situation.
C2H6O = ethanol (bp ~78°C, fizzes with sodium) OR dimethyl ether (gas, bp ~ -24°C, ignores sodium).
Same formula, wildly different chemistry — one has an O-H bond a metal can attack, the other doesn't.
Isomer counts explode: C4H10 has 2, C10H22 has 75, larger alkanes run into billions.
Railway coaches: reorder them → structural isomer. Keep order, flip how a coach faces → stereoisomer.
The master split — two questions in order
Q1: Are the atoms connected the same way? No → structural isomers.
Q2: same connectivity but different in space? Yes → stereoisomers. Always compare the FORMULA first.

segments_english.text: Isomerism is one of the highest-value ideas in organic chemistry, so let's build it from a single sharp intuition.

Two people can share the same identity-card data, same name, same age, same town, and still be completely different individuals because of how their lives are arranged. Isomers are molecules in exactly that situation: the same molecular formula, yet different compounds.

The textbook pair makes it vivid. C two H six O can be ethanol, a liquid boiling near seventy-eight degrees that fizzes violently with sodium, or dimethyl ether, a gas boiling near minus twenty-four degrees that ignores sodium completely.

<curious>Same formula, wildly different molecules. And the gap isn't a small matter of degree, it's a matter of kind: one has an oxygen-hydrogen bond a reactive metal can attack, the other simply doesn't.
The number of possible isomers also balloons astonishingly fast. C four H ten has just two isomers, but C ten H twenty-two already has seventy-five, and modestly larger alkanes run into the billions.

Think of a set of railway coaches. Reconnect them in a different order and you have a structurally different train, that's structural isomerism, a difference in connectivity. Keep the connectivity identical but flip which way a coach faces, and you have stereoisomerism, a difference in spatial arrangement.
So the whole subject reduces to two questions asked in a strict order.
Question one: are the atoms connected the same way? If no, they're structural isomers, full stop.

Question two only matters if connectivity is identical: are the atoms then arranged differently in space? If yes, they're stereoisomers. And notice the discipline: you always compare the molecular formula first, because without an identical formula they aren't isomers at all.

segments_hinglish.text: Isomerism organic chemistry के सबसे high-value ideas में से एक है, तो चलो इसे एक sharp intuition से बनाते हैं।

दो लोग एक ही identity-card data share कर सकते हैं, same name, same age, same town, और फिर भी बिलकुल अलग individuals हो सकते हैं क्योंकि उनकी lives कैसे arranged हैं। Isomers molecules बिलकुल उसी situation में हैं: same molecular formula, फिर भी अलग compounds।

Textbook pair इसे vivid बना देती है। C two H six O या तो ethanol हो सकता है, एक liquid जो seventy-eight degrees के पास boil होता है और sodium के साथ violently fizz करता है, या dimethyl ether, एक gas जो minus twenty-four degrees के पास boil होता है और sodium को पूरी तरह ignore करता है।
<curious>Same formula, बिलकुल अलग molecules। और ये gap degree का छोटा मामला नहीं, kind का मामला है: एक के पास oxygen-hydrogen bond है जिस पर reactive metal attack कर सकता है, दूसरे के पास बस नहीं है।

Possible isomers की संख्या भी हैरान करने वाली speed से balloon करती है। C four H ten के सिर्फ़ two isomers हैं, पर C ten H twenty-two के पहले ही seventy-five, और थोड़े बड़े alkanes billions में पहुँच जाते हैं।

Railway coaches का एक set सोचो। इन्हें अलग order में reconnect करो और आपके पास एक structurally अलग train है, ये structural isomerism है, connectivity का फ़र्क़। Connectivity same रखो पर एक coach किस तरफ़ face करता है वो flip करो, और आपके पास stereoisomerism है, spatial arrangement का फ़र्क़।
तो पूरा subject एक strict order में पूछे दो questions में सिमट जाता है।
Question one: क्या atoms same तरीक़े से connected हैं? अगर नहीं, तो वो structural isomers हैं, बस।

Question two तभी matter करता है जब connectivity identical हो: क्या atoms फिर space में अलग arranged हैं? अगर हाँ, तो वो stereoisomers हैं। और discipline देखो: आप हमेशा पहले molecular formula compare करते हो, क्योंकि identical formula के बिना वो isomers हैं ही नहीं।

board_content.text: Structural isomerism — six types
Chain: carbon-skeleton branching. n-butane vs 2-methylpropane (C4H10).
Position: position of a group / multiple bond. but-1-ene vs but-2-ene (C4H8).
Functional: nature of the functional group. alcohol vs ether (C2H6O).
Metamerism: alkyl distribution around a divalent group (-O-, -S-, -NH-, -CO-). methoxypropane vs ethoxyethane (C4H10O).
Ring-chain: open chain vs closed ring. but-1-ene vs cyclobutane (C4H8), both DoU = 1.
Tautomerism: dynamic 1,3-H shift. keto ⇌ enol (a real equilibrium, not two isolable substances).
Functional-group pairs to memorise: alcohols ↔ ethers, aldehydes ↔ ketones, acids ↔ esters.

segments_english.text: Branch one of the tree is structural isomerism, and it comes in exactly six standard flavours. Learn to tell them apart, because exam questions live on that distinction.
Chain isomerism changes the backbone. C four H ten is either the unbranched n-butane or the branched two-methylpropane, same atoms, different skeleton.
Position isomerism keeps the skeleton fixed and just moves a group or a multiple bond along it. But-one-ene and but-two-ene differ only in where the double bond sits.
Functional-group isomerism swaps the functional group entirely for the same formula. C two H six O as an alcohol versus an ether is the model case.

Metamerism is narrower: the same divalent linkage, an oxygen, sulphur, N H or carbonyl, carries different alkyl groups on its two sides. Methoxypropane and ethoxyethane are both C four H ten O ethers that split the carbons differently around the oxygen.

Ring-chain isomerism pits an open chain against a ring of the same formula. But-one-ene and cyclobutane are both C four H eight with one degree of unsaturation, but one spends it on a double bond and the other on a ring.

<curious>Tautomerism is the odd one out because it's dynamic, not static. A mobile hydrogen shuttles back and forth in a one-three shift, so the keto and enol forms exist in a real equilibrium rather than as two bottles on a shelf. Most simple carbonyls sit overwhelmingly on the keto side.
The three functional-group pairs worth memorising cold: alcohols with ethers, aldehydes with ketones, and carboxylic acids with esters.

segments_hinglish.text: Tree की branch one है structural isomerism, और ये exactly छह standard flavours में आती है। इन्हें अलग पहचानना सीखो, क्योंकि exam questions इसी distinction पर जीते हैं।
Chain isomerism backbone बदलता है। C four H ten या तो unbranched n-butane है या branched two-methylpropane, same atoms, अलग skeleton।
Position isomerism skeleton fix रखता है और बस एक group या multiple bond को उस पर move करता है। But-one-ene और but-two-ene सिर्फ़ इसमें अलग हैं कि double bond कहाँ बैठता है।
Functional-group isomerism same formula के लिए functional group को पूरा swap कर देता है। C two H six O एक alcohol बनाम एक ether model case है।

Metamerism narrower है: same divalent linkage, एक oxygen, sulphur, N H या carbonyl, अपने दोनों तरफ़ अलग alkyl groups रखता है। Methoxypropane और ethoxyethane दोनों C four H ten O ethers हैं जो oxygen के around carbons को अलग तरह से split करते हैं।

Ring-chain isomerism एक open chain को same formula के ring के ख़िलाफ़ खड़ा करता है। But-one-ene और cyclobutane दोनों C four H eight हैं एक degree of unsaturation के साथ, पर एक इसे double bond पर ख़र्च करता है और दूसरा ring पर।

<curious>Tautomerism odd one out है क्योंकि ये dynamic है, static नहीं। एक mobile hydrogen one-three shift में आगे-पीछे shuttle करता है, तो keto और enol forms एक real equilibrium में रहते हैं, shelf पर दो bottles की तरह नहीं। ज़्यादातर simple carbonyls overwhelmingly keto side पर बैठते हैं।
तीन functional-group pairs जो पक्के याद करने लायक़ हैं: alcohols with ethers, aldehydes with ketones, और carboxylic acids with esters।

board_content.text: Stereoisomerism I — geometrical (cis-trans / E-Z)
Arises from restricted rotation about a C=C or a ring.

board_content.text: cis = like groups on the same side; trans = opposite sides.
Needs restricted rotation AND two different groups on each restricted carbon.
Fails if either carbon bears two identical groups — flipping them gives the same molecule (ethene, propene).
E/Z removes cis/trans ambiguity: rank groups by CIP priority (atomic number first).
Higher-priority groups same side → Z; opposite sides → E. Priority by atomic number, not size.

segments_english.text: Now branch two, stereoisomerism, where connectivity is identical and only the arrangement in space differs. We'll take geometrical isomerism first.
Geometrical isomerism arises from restricted rotation, either about a carbon-carbon double bond or around a ring, because those can't freely spin the way a single bond can.
The board shows the classic pair: cis and trans but-two-ene, identical connectivity, different geometry.
In the cis form the like groups sit on the same side of the double bond; in the trans form they sit on opposite sides.
<curious>But there's a strict entry condition. You need restricted rotation and, crucially, two different groups on each of the restricted carbons.

If either carbon carries two identical groups, geometrical isomerism simply vanishes, because flipping two identical groups gives you back the very same molecule. That's why ethene and propene show none.

When all four groups differ, cis and trans become ambiguous, same side as what? So chemists use the E-Z system, ranking the two groups on each carbon by C I P priority, which starts from atomic number.

The rule then reads cleanly: if the two higher-priority groups lie on the same side it's Z, on opposite sides it's E. And priority is set by atomic number, not by how bulky a group looks, so a single bromine outranks an entire carbon chain.

segments_hinglish.text: अब branch two, stereoisomerism, जहाँ connectivity identical है और सिर्फ़ space में arrangement अलग है। हम पहले geometrical isomerism लेंगे।
Geometrical isomerism restricted rotation से आती है, या तो एक carbon-carbon double bond के around या एक ring के around, क्योंकि ये single bond की तरह freely घूम नहीं सकते।
Board classic pair दिखाता है: cis और trans but-two-ene, identical connectivity, अलग geometry।
Cis form में like groups double bond के same side पर बैठते हैं; trans form में वो opposite sides पर बैठते हैं।
<curious>पर एक strict entry condition है। आपको restricted rotation चाहिए और, सबसे ज़रूरी, हर restricted carbon पर दो अलग groups चाहिए।

अगर कोई carbon दो identical groups रखता है, तो geometrical isomerism बस ग़ायब हो जाती है, क्योंकि दो identical groups flip करने पर वही molecule वापस मिलता है। इसीलिए ethene और propene कोई नहीं दिखाते।

जब चारों groups अलग हों, तो cis और trans ambiguous हो जाते हैं, किसके same side? तो chemists E-Z system use करते हैं, हर carbon पर दोनों groups को C I P priority से rank करके, जो atomic number से शुरू होती है।

Rule फिर साफ़ पढ़ता है: अगर दोनों higher-priority groups same side पर हों तो Z, opposite sides पर हों तो E। और priority atomic number से तय होती है, group कितना bulky दिखता है उससे नहीं, तो एक अकेला bromine पूरी carbon chain को outrank करता है।

board_content.text: Stereoisomerism II — optical (chirality)
Chirality: a molecule non-superimposable on its mirror image, like left and right hands.
