board_content.text: Aniline meets both conditions for steam distillation: volatile in steam AND immiscible with water.
Combined vapour pressure of aniline + water reaches atmospheric BELOW aniline's own boiling point.
So aniline distils over with the steam at a gentler temperature; the non-volatile impurity stays behind.
Answer: steam distillation.
Board habit: name the method AND state the two physical conditions that justify it — reasoning earns the marks.

segments_english.text: A board-level purification question about aniline, which comes contaminated with a non-volatile impurity.
We're told aniline is steam-volatile and immiscible with water, and asked which purification method fits and why.
The board sketches the apparatus: steam is passed into the mixture, and the aniline travels over with it into the condenser.
Aniline meets both conditions for steam distillation exactly: it's appreciably volatile in steam, and it doesn't mix with water, while the impurity is non-volatile.
Here's the physics. Because the two are immiscible, their vapour pressures simply add, so the combined vapour pressure reaches atmospheric pressure below aniline's own boiling point.
So the aniline distils over together with the steam at a gentler temperature, and the non-volatile impurity is left behind in the flask.
The answer, then, is steam distillation.

<curious>The board habit that earns full marks: don't just name the method. State the two physical conditions that justify it, steam-volatility and water-immiscibility, because the examiner rewards the reasoning, not the keyword.

segments_hinglish.text: Aniline के बारे में एक board-level purification question, जो एक non-volatile impurity के साथ contaminated आता है।
हमें बताया गया कि aniline steam-volatile और water से immiscible है, और पूछा गया कौन सा purification method fit होता है और क्यों।
Board apparatus sketch करता है: steam को mixture में pass किया जाता है, और aniline उसके साथ condenser में चला जाता है।
Aniline steam distillation की दोनों conditions बिलकुल meet करता है: ये steam में appreciably volatile है, और ये water से mix नहीं होता, जबकि impurity non-volatile है।
यहाँ physics है। क्योंकि दोनों immiscible हैं, उनके vapour pressures बस जुड़ जाते हैं, तो combined vapour pressure aniline के अपने boiling point से नीचे atmospheric pressure तक पहुँच जाता है।
तो aniline steam के साथ एक gentler temperature पर distil हो जाता है, और non-volatile impurity flask में पीछे रह जाती है।
तो जवाब है steam distillation।

<curious>वो board habit जो full marks दिलाती है: सिर्फ़ method का नाम मत बताओ। उसे justify करने वाली दो physical conditions बताओ, steam-volatility और water-immiscibility, क्योंकि examiner reasoning को reward करता है, keyword को नहीं।

title: Worked example — read a Lassaigne colour (NEET)

board_content.text: Worked example — read a Lassaigne colour (N E E T)
A sodium fusion extract gives a blood-red colour with ferric ions. What does the compound contain?
Blood-red with Fe3+ comes from thiocyanate (SCN-).
Thiocyanate forms ONLY when both N and S are present (they combine during fusion → NaSCN).
Answer: both nitrogen and sulphur.
Trap: reading 'red' as the nitrogen-alone test. Nitrogen alone gives Prussian BLUE, not red.
Memorise: blue = N; blood-red = N and S together.
One colour cleanly distinguishes 'N only' from 'N and S' — a classic one-line NEET item.

segments_english.text: A one-line N E E T item that tests whether you truly know the Lassaigne colours.
A compound's sodium fusion extract gives a blood-red colour with ferric ions. What does that tell us the compound contains?
That blood-red colour with iron three ions comes specifically from the thiocyanate ion.
And thiocyanate only forms when both nitrogen and sulphur are present in the compound, because the two combine during the sodium fusion to give sodium thiocyanate.
So the answer is that the compound contains both nitrogen and sulphur.
<curious>Here's the trap: reading red as the test for nitrogen alone. Nitrogen on its own gives Prussian blue, not red. The blood-red is the combined nitrogen-and-sulphur signature.
So memorise the pair cleanly: blue means nitrogen; blood-red means nitrogen and sulphur together.
That single colour cleanly separates nitrogen only from nitrogen and sulphur, which is exactly why it's such a reliable one-line question.

segments_hinglish.text: एक one-line N E E T item जो test करता है कि आप सच में Lassaigne colours जानते हो।
एक compound का sodium fusion extract ferric ions के साथ एक blood-red colour देता है। ये हमें क्या बताता है कि compound में क्या है?
वो blood-red colour iron three ions के साथ specifically thiocyanate ion से आता है।
और thiocyanate सिर्फ़ तब बनता है जब compound में nitrogen और sulphur दोनों present हों, क्योंकि दोनों sodium fusion के दौरान मिलकर sodium thiocyanate देते हैं।
तो जवाब है कि compound में nitrogen और sulphur दोनों हैं।
<curious>यहाँ trap है: red को अकेले nitrogen का test पढ़ना। अकेला nitrogen Prussian blue देता है, red नहीं। Blood-red combined nitrogen-and-sulphur signature है।
तो pair को साफ़ याद कर लो: blue मतलब nitrogen; blood-red मतलब nitrogen और sulphur साथ में।
वो अकेला colour nitrogen only को nitrogen और sulphur से साफ़ अलग करता है, इसीलिए ये इतना reliable one-line question है।

title: Worked example — Liebig C & H estimation (JEE Main)

board_content.text: Worked example — Liebig C & H estimation (J E E Main)
0.30 g of a compound on combustion gives 0.44 g CO2 and 0.18 g H2O. Find %C and %H.
If oxygen is sought: %O = 100 - 40.0 - 6.67 = 53.33% (by difference).
All carbon → CO2 (12/44 of it is C); all hydrogen → H2O (2/18 of it is H).
Couple the mass-fraction idea with the 'oxygen by difference' closure — the standard JEE Main format.
Values script-verified: %C = 40.0, %H = 6.67.

segments_english.text: A standard J E E Main combustion numerical using Liebig's method for carbon and hydrogen.

Zero point three zero grams of a compound, on complete combustion, gives zero point four four grams of carbon dioxide and zero point one eight grams of water. Find the percentages of carbon and hydrogen.
For carbon: twelve over forty-four, times zero point four four over zero point three zero, times one hundred, comes out to forty point zero percent.
For hydrogen: two over eighteen, times zero point one eight over zero point three zero, times one hundred, comes out to six point six seven percent.
If oxygen is also wanted, get it by difference: one hundred minus forty minus six point six seven leaves fifty-three point three three percent.

<curious>The logic underneath: all the carbon ends up in the carbon dioxide, and twelve out of every forty-four mass units of carbon dioxide is carbon. Likewise all the hydrogen ends up in water, two out of every eighteen mass units being hydrogen.
So this couples the mass-fraction idea with the oxygen-by-difference closure, which is exactly the standard J E E Main estimation format.
And the values check out: carbon is forty point zero percent and hydrogen is six point six seven percent.

segments_hinglish.text: Carbon और hydrogen के लिए Liebig's method use करता एक standard J E E Main combustion numerical।
एक compound के zero point three zero grams, complete combustion पर, zero point four four grams carbon dioxide और zero point one eight grams water देते हैं। Carbon और hydrogen के percentages निकालो।
Carbon के लिए: twelve over forty-four, into zero point four four over zero point three zero, into one hundred, आता है forty point zero percent।
Hydrogen के लिए: two over eighteen, into zero point one eight over zero point three zero, into one hundred, आता है six point six seven percent।
अगर oxygen भी चाहिए, तो difference से निकालो: one hundred minus forty minus six point six seven बचता है fifty-three point three three percent।

<curious>नीचे की logic: सारा carbon carbon dioxide में जाता है, और carbon dioxide के हर forty-four mass units में से twelve carbon है। वैसे ही सारा hydrogen water में जाता है, हर eighteen mass units में से two hydrogen होता है।
तो ये mass-fraction idea को oxygen-by-difference closure के साथ जोड़ता है, जो बिलकुल standard J E E Main estimation format है।
और values सही निकलती हैं: carbon forty point zero percent और hydrogen six point six seven percent।

title: Worked example — Dumas N estimation (JEE Advanced)

board_content.text: Worked example — Dumas N estimation (J E E Advanced)
0.28 g gives 50 mL of N2 over water at 300 K and 745 mm. Aqueous tension at 300 K = 25 mm. Find %N.
Correct for water vapour: P_dry = 745 - 25 = 720 mm.
Moles N2 = 43.1 / 22400; moles N = 2×; mass N = moles × 14 ≈ 0.0539 g.
The marks hide in the aqueous-tension correction — subtract 25 mm BEFORE the STP conversion.
Values script-verified: %N ≈ 19.24%.

segments_english.text: The J E E Advanced numerical is a Dumas nitrogen estimation, and it hides its marks in one easily-missed correction.

Zero point two eight grams of a compound gives fifty millilitres of nitrogen gas, collected over water at three hundred kelvin and seven hundred forty-five millimetres pressure. The aqueous tension at that temperature is twenty-five millimetres. Find the percentage of nitrogen.
First, correct the pressure for water vapour. The dry pressure is seven hundred forty-five minus twenty-five, which is seven hundred twenty millimetres.

Now convert the volume to S T P. Fifty millilitres, times seven hundred twenty over seven hundred sixty for pressure, times two hundred seventy-three over three hundred for temperature, gives forty-three point one millilitres.

Divide forty-three point one by twenty-two thousand four hundred to get the moles of nitrogen gas; double that for moles of nitrogen atoms; then multiply by fourteen to get the mass of nitrogen, about zero point zero five four grams.
Finally, the percentage of nitrogen is that mass over zero point two eight, times one hundred, which is nineteen point two four percent.

<whisper>And here's exactly where the marks hide: the aqueous-tension correction. Forgetting to subtract those twenty-five millimetres inflates the volume and the final answer, so always reduce the gas-over-water pressure before the S T P conversion.
The value checks out at about nineteen point two four percent nitrogen.

segments_hinglish.text: J E E Advanced numerical एक Dumas nitrogen estimation है, और ये अपने marks एक आसानी से छूट जाने वाली correction में छुपाता है।

एक compound के zero point two eight grams fifty millilitres nitrogen gas देते हैं, water के ऊपर three hundred kelvin और seven hundred forty-five millimetres pressure पर collected। उस temperature पर aqueous tension twenty-five millimetres है। Percentage of nitrogen निकालो।
पहले, pressure को water vapour के लिए correct करो। Dry pressure है seven hundred forty-five minus twenty-five, जो seven hundred twenty millimetres है।

अब volume को S T P में convert करो। Fifty millilitres, into seven hundred twenty over seven hundred sixty pressure के लिए, into two hundred seventy-three over three hundred temperature के लिए, देता है forty-three point one millilitres।

Forty-three point one को twenty-two thousand four hundred से भाग दो nitrogen gas के moles के लिए; उसे double करो nitrogen atoms के moles के लिए; फिर fourteen से गुणा करो nitrogen की mass के लिए, लगभग zero point zero five four grams।
आख़िर में, percentage of nitrogen है वो mass zero point two eight के ऊपर, into one hundred, जो nineteen point two four percent है।

<whisper>और यहीं exactly marks छुपते हैं: aqueous-tension correction। उन twenty-five millimetres को घटाना भूलना volume और final answer को बढ़ा देता है, तो हमेशा S T P conversion से पहले gas-over-water pressure कम करो।
Value लगभग nineteen point two four percent nitrogen पर सही निकलती है।

board_content.text: Pitfalls & pro-tips — Purification & Analysis
Pitfall 1 (ORG-PUR-METHOD-MATCH): match the technique to the property that differs — b.p.→distillation, solubility→crystallisation, sublimes→sublimation.
Pitfall 2 (ORG-QUAL-N-VS-NS): Prussian blue = nitrogen; blood-red with Fe3+ = nitrogen AND sulphur together.
Pitfall 3 (ORG-QUANT-METHOD-ELEMENT): Carius → halogen/S; Dumas & Kjeldahl → N; Liebig → C & H.
Pitfall 4 (ORG-QUANT-AQ-TENSION): for gas-over-water, subtract the water-vapour pressure before converting to STP.
Pitfall 5 (ORG-QUANT-O-BY-DIFF): never estimate oxygen directly — get it by difference.
Pro-tip (numericals): memorise 12/44 (C), 2/18 (H), and the 1.4 Kjeldahl factor → most %-composition problems fall in one line.

segments_english.text: <curious>Before we finish, here is every formula from the chapter gathered in one place, so you can revise them in one sweep.
The homologous general formulae: alkanes are C n H two n plus two, alkenes C n H two n, and alkynes C n H two n minus two.
The ketone series shares the aldehyde's formula, C n H two n O.
Degree of unsaturation is two n plus two plus q minus m, all over two, counting rings plus pi bonds.
The maximum number of stereoisomers from n stereocentres is two raised to the power n, an upper bound only.
The chromatography retardation factor is the component's distance over the solvent front's distance.
For combustion: percentage of carbon uses twelve over forty-four, and percentage of hydrogen uses two over eighteen, each times the product mass over the compound mass times one hundred.

And for the others: Kjeldahl nitrogen uses the one point four factor times normality times volume over mass, while Carius halogen uses the atomic-mass over silver-halide-mass ratio. Oxygen, remember, always comes by difference.

title: Cheat sheet — Organic Chemistry: Basic Principles

board_content.text: Cheat sheet — Organic Chemistry: Basic Principles
Foundations: vertex = C, heteroatoms explicit; classify skeleton (acyclic/cyclic → carbocyclic: alicyclic/aromatic, vs heterocyclic) then functional group; homologues differ by CH2.
Hybridization: σ-count (+ lone pairs) = 4/3/2 → sp3/sp2/sp (109.5°/120°/180°). More %s → shorter, stronger, more acidic, more electronegative.
Naming: lock the suffix (seniority) → longest chain through it → lowest locant to that group → substituents alphabetical; tie-break by first point of difference.
Isomerism: connect first, then arrange. Geometrical needs two different groups on each restricted C; chiral = 4 different groups + no symmetry; racemic (external) vs meso (internal).

Mechanisms: homolytic → radicals (fishhook), heterolytic → ions (full arrow); nucleophile electron-rich, electrophile electron-poor (density, not charge); stability: resonance → hyperconjugation → induction.
Analysis: match method to the differing property; Lassaigne (blue = N, red = N&S); Liebig C&H · Dumas/Kjeldahl N · Carius X/S; oxygen by difference.
Memory anchors: 'vertex & end are carbon' · 'suffix first' · 'connect first, then arrange' · 'cation planar, anion pyramidal' · 'blue is N, red is N&S'.
